Transphobia

By: Tarryn Crossman | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The reality of transgendered teenagers in South Africa

Unique Selling Point:
In 2014 Gender dynamix did a study with 17 trans youths, the results of which shows a society ignorant and unaccepting of transgender people. As well as serious gaps in schools and state medical procedures available to young trans people.

Asive was born a boy in rural Eastern Cape, but she identified as a girl from the age of 10. Her parents thought she was bewitched and potencially was having the calling to become a sangoma. At 16 she no longer wanted to wear her male assigned school uniform and wore a dress to school. She also refused to be sent to the bush for her male initiation. The school kicked her out and her parents threatened to do the same, until the commission for Gender Equality in the Eastern Cape fought for her to be allowed to wear what she wanted, "within reason", to school.

Her story is not unique for transgendered teenager in South Africa, especially in peri-urban and rural areas. There are so many issues with the education system in these areas that education about transgender teens is not a big priority.

Boy in the eastern cape, anonymous for now, he was the first teenager to get transgender affirming surgery in South Africa. He had both breasts removed. It was a legal battle to get him the surgery, as surgery is only given to people over 18.
Or

Angelique she was 14 when the study was done, she is 16.
When she was a boy identifying as a girl she was bullied at school. Boys threw stones and spat at her. Her mother fought for her right to attend a new school as a girl, but her identity was kept a secret for her own safety. She was allowed to use the staff toilet to avoid persecution. This act of kindness by the school staff was in fact just more segregating. According to the constitution schools should in fact have gender neutral toilets or trans pupils should feel safe to use the toilet that aligns with their gender identity

Some of the biggest issues is the these gender aligning or sexual preferences are not discussed in school at all. They should be a part of life orientation.

In South Africa preteens are not allowed hormone treatment, they can however go onto puberty blockers. Going through puberty for a child that already identifies as trans can be extremely traumatic.
They can only official get hormone therapy at 16 and surgery after 18.
The waiting list for surgery at the Groote schuur trans clinic is 25 years
To get the surgery done privately costs between R40000 - R60000

Schools

the psychology of being trans.
Can a 10 year child really know they are trans.
Hormone treatment available from the state - costs
Surgical procedures available from the state - costs

Education - do we speak to the national ministry for education?

Press Release:


Transphobia
Transgender children face major barriers when trying to navigate the school system, such as accessing bathrooms, wearing gender-specific school uniforms
and being accepted onto school teams. These teens find it harder to adjust to an educational structure which isn’t designed to accept their gender
identities. Carte Blanche asks whether schools are fully prepared to receive transgender children.

Script:

1 00:00 Introduction of Asive
Asive: at school there was a huge terrific reaction when I came wearing a girls uniform. My principle said, “what's happening?” She chased me out
2 00:11 Sam- character Sam: I still walked into school the one and there were these group of dudes that walked pass me and they were like “yoh it’s a dude in a dress” oh gosh.
3 00:20 Sam’s mother - Kate They had an issue with his sexuality and they wanted to know if he's a hermaphrodite, how could they have a strange person at their school.
4 00:28 V/O John With a rising awareness around the constitutional rights of transgendered teens in the school system, we look into the plight of two transgendered teenagers in the Eastern Cape.
5 00:38 John introduces Sam the character Sam not his real name is a transgender male. He was born a girl but soon he discovered that he didn’t belong to the body that he was born into
6 00:48 Sam It started as far back as I can remember, I didn’t like wearing dresses I would rather run around in my underwear than rather put a dress on.
7 00:57 John V/O Asive is a transgender female who was persecuted by her community and rejected by her family when she came out as being transgender
8 01:05 Asive I'm from the eastern cape in a little village called Qumbu called Qanqu. I was grew by my grandmother. I was born as a male and transitioned into a girl
9 01:20 Sam speaks about puberty Pre puberty was not that bad, my mom let me wear whatever I clothes I would like and yeah I just if people didn’t know me I would introduce myself as a boy and they would not know better
10 01:37 Asive speaks about puberty When I experienced puberty I started hating my body. From the inside I was sure that I was girl but I didn’t know what was happening, you just have something at the back of your mind that terrifies you, that says I Hate this body.
11 01:53 Sam I don't ever think about that time or that I was a girl. I don't connect at all with being a girl

12 02:04 V/O What does it actually mean to be transgender? Dr Taylor is a child and adolescence psychiatrists who specialist in gender identity development

13 02:14 Interview with Dr Taylor and john John: is this biological or environmental?
Dr. Taylor: In the past psychiatrist did think it was environment and parents somehow brought up their children in the wrong way and this has been very closely studied that how you raise your child produces a transgender child

14 02:35 Kate – Sam’s mother Kate: by age 4 we sort of knew and by age 14 I asked Seth “are you in the wrong body” and he said ‘yes mom’. Initially it was did I do something wrong during my pregnancy? But then I did a lot of reading and research and there's nothing you can do it happens.
15 02:53 Dr Taylor People who feel they are sex of their bodies or have a gender of their body. A male born with a make body and who feels they are male is cisgendered where as a male who feels they are actually female is transgendered. Children as young as 2 or 3 have developed a sense of gender identity.
16 03:14 John Link Both Sam and Asive were persecuted by these schools for being transgender. They reach out to the commission of gender equality where Kerry Oosthuizen was the lawyer to fight their constitution rights for freedom of expression, equality, education and most of all dignity.
17 03:31 Kerry Oosthuysen – Lawyer In south Africa I'm speaking specifically in my province especially in the Eastern cape, school sometimes believe they are their own sovereign state that dictate to the students what they think is correct, but at the end of the day there is a constitution, laws and guidelines. The interest of the child is paramount,
18 03:52 Kate Then as he got older and his body changed the anxiety started coming and the anger. Many morning I had to drag him out of bed, try to get him put his uniform on, drag him to school and sit outside school maybe up to half an hour saying ‘ please go into school, please go into school’ he just did not want to go into that school.
19 04:13 Sam At that point I was seeing a therapist. I did try and tell him like you know I had to know wear this uniform at school and it didn’t feel like me it just not what I wanted to be doing or how I wanted to present. The one-day I sort of just went to school in pants, the principle pretty much denied that.
20 04:39 Asive When I entered the gate my principle said, “what's happening? Why are you wearing girls uniform? “They just saw me as an inhumane or something or animal because it was a first time they see someone like me. She said I must go out and change the uniform and come back wearing the uniform that I used to wear. I tried to explain to him that ‘no this is what's happening and I don't feel comfortable in boys uniform” and then she didn’t tolerate any of it
21 05:11 Sam My mom went and had a meeting with them and it didn’t turn out very well
22 05:17 Kate I went to the principle and I said ‘ please we just want to wear a pair of pants’. My child is not identifying as a girl he’s identifying as a boy. The principle said that the governing body refused and said, “no it’s not going to happen”. Then I was asked to please remove him from the school.
23 05:34 Kerry So when I met them you could see the suffering. The department of education got involved and they sent out a circular to schools pre-warning them of such conduct that it’s a violation of the constitution and national guidelines of school uniforms policy and various other p0ieces of legislation
24 05:58 John V/O Gender Dynamix a Cape town based NGO that offers support to transgender people. After being inundated with calls from the parents of potentially transgendered people they did a study on transgendered youth.
25 06:11 John interview with Siphe – Gender Dynamix John: what are some of the more significant finding you came across in your study?
Siphe: two most predominate findings were actually around bulling transgender individuals as well as barriers to accessing things like bathrooms, school uniforms and school teams. Just ostracize these children at a time when everyone in essence wants to fit in
John: do you have the support of the national department of basic education?
Siphe: because of the finding of our youth and transgender studies we actually created the gender identity school booklet to try an elevate a number of descrimitary and lack of knowledge barriers that exist. However because gender identity in schools hasn’t been rolled out nationally per say in the LO curriculum its on a voluntary basis so we arable to work with schools that want to know about gender identity and expression but we are not at a national level yet.
26 07:02 John Voice over Even though this crucial book that exists its not yet a mandatory part of the national school circulum.in gendered school uniforms continue to create anxiety for transgender teens across the country.
27 07:14 Kerry In my view school should adopt a gender-neutral policy with regards to school uniforms because then it wont be an issue.
28 07:23 Sam I feel the school system made it harder I mean if I just told them I would like to wear pants and they say okay you know that would’ve saved a lot of stress.
29 07:34 John V/O Transgender youth are rejected by society at large go through such depression and anxiety the suicide rate this community is at a staggering 41%
30 07:47 Asive You see when you are transgender you have to bottle up your feelings, you have to hide how you feel sometimes because I don't know its too much yes
31 08:05 Sam Its strange you know to think that just being another gender really stressed me out all of that. It really did like I said I cain’t every really explain it to myself
32 08:21 Link John Sam was the first teenager to get top surgery in south Africa at 16 unfortunately Asive treatments has not been as successful. There are only two government hospitals offering gender-affirming care and they are based in Cape Town and Johannesburg. The waiting list for surgery is 25 years.
33 08:38 Asive The problem is that I couldn’t find an endocrinologist in the eastern cape so I was self medicating. The hormones I was talking from women who have menopause they were expensive so when I’m run out of hormones I used conceptive.
34 08:54 Link John When one talks about transgender teens getting gender affirming treatment people often argue that they are not ready to make such a bold decision but statistically it is proven that 80% of teenagers who receive hormones treatment during puberty never want to return to the gender they were born as
35 09:11 Dr. Taylor If you leave them until they are 18 which is what everyone used to do by that stage either they might’ve killed themselves. Also if you leave it till 18, these people need masses amount of surgery and all sort of things to change their body to look like the opposite sex. The truth is most adult transgender who have not had the hormones as teenagers never really passes the opposite sex
36 09:36 Sam I was so lucky because my family was support; most of my friends were supportive.
37 09:43 Kim We fought and it was a long journey but we got there. Today he is happy well-adjusted young man.
38 09:52 Asive If I could still speak to my granny I would say I'm still that person who has memories but I discovered myself that I'm this person and I'm just a child and I'm still their child and I still love them.
